# Komposite News

> Komposite News is an independent digital publication covering artificial intelligence, blockchain, digital assets, enterprise technology, cybersecurity, fintech and capital markets. It writes for executives, founders, investors, developers and policy professionals who need to understand how technology and finance are changing each other, and prioritizes reporting and analysis over hype.

- News stories, pieces labeled Analysis and pieces labeled Opinion are clearly distinguished.
- Information is attributed to sources wherever possible and claims are verified before publication; sponsored content is always labeled.
- Corrected articles carry a note describing what was wrong and when it was fixed.
- Komposite News uses AI tools to help research, draft and edit stories; every story is checked against its listed sources and approved by an editor before it goes live. Bylines name the desk or house byline responsible; they are not always individual reporters (see https://kompositenews.com/editorial-standards/#how-we-use-ai).
- A selection of coverage is also published in Spanish under /es/.
- All articles are free to read. A plain-text copy of the key stories is at https://kompositenews.com/llms-full.txt.

- [Fintech](https://kompositenews.com/fintech/): payments, banking technology and financial infrastructure
- [Crypto](https://kompositenews.com/crypto/): digital assets, stablecoins and crypto markets
- [Blockchain](https://kompositenews.com/blockchain/): blockchain infrastructure reporting and analysis
- [Cybersecurity](https://kompositenews.com/cybersecurity/): breaches, threats and security practice
- [Policy](https://kompositenews.com/policy/): regulation, legislation and policy
- [Culture](https://kompositenews.com/culture/): culture and media
- [Music](https://kompositenews.com/music/): music coverage
- [Opinion](https://kompositenews.com/opinion/): labeled opinion and columns
- [The Divide](https://kompositenews.com/the-divide/): one major issue each edition, argued from the left and from the right
- [Latest](https://kompositenews.com/latest/): all reporting in chronological order
- [Authors](https://kompositenews.com/authors/): the newsroom and contributors
- [Español](https://kompositenews.com/es/): Spanish-language edition (selected coverage)

## Key guides and analysis

- [What buyers actually do with an SBOM](https://kompositenews.com/cybersecurity/sbom-what-buyers-do-with-it/): Software bills of materials are now routinely produced and routinely ignored, and the gap between generating one and acting on it is where the risk sits.
- [What an attestation must prove](https://kompositenews.com/crypto/what-an-attestation-must-prove/): Stablecoin law requires monthly examination of reserves, and the open rulemaking question is what level of assurance that examination must actually deliver.
- [What a seed round now requires](https://kompositenews.com/startups/what-a-seed-round-now-requires/): Seed rounds now arrive after revenue and retention evidence that once belonged to Series A, and the gap between rounds has stretched past two years.
- [AI in the order flow: what machine trading is doing to volatility](https://kompositenews.com/markets/volatility-market-structure-ai-trading/): Adaptive execution and model-driven strategies are changing intraday dynamics in ways researchers are only beginning to measure.
- [Machine identity sprawl becomes security's biggest inventory problem](https://kompositenews.com/cybersecurity/identity-machine-workloads/): Service accounts, API keys, and agent credentials now outnumber human identities many times over, and governance is racing the growth.
- [Enterprises write the rulebook for AI-generated code](https://kompositenews.com/ai/ai-coding-tools-enterprise-standards/): Provenance tracking, review gates, and dependency policies are turning AI coding assistance from a developer perk into governed infrastructure.
- [AI evaluation grows from afterthought to budget line](https://kompositenews.com/ai/ai-evaluation-becomes-budget-line/): Enterprises deploying models at scale are formalizing evaluation the way they once formalized QA, and a vendor category is forming around it.
- [Power availability becomes the master constraint on computing](https://kompositenews.com/technology/power-constraints-shape-computing/): Grid interconnection queues, not chip supply, now set the timeline for new capacity, and the industry is reorganizing around electrons.
- [Shadow AI becomes the new shadow IT](https://kompositenews.com/business/shadow-ai-governance-problem/): Employees are routing work through unsanctioned AI tools faster than policies can name them, and enterprises are choosing between control and visibility.
- [Instant payments become table stakes in B2B](https://kompositenews.com/fintech/instant-payments-b2b-standard/): Real-time rails are moving from consumer novelty to supplier expectation, and the software layer on top is where the margin lives.
- [Stablecoin Reserve reporting converges on common standards](https://kompositenews.com/crypto/stablecoin-reserve-transparency-standards/): Monthly attestations are giving way to standardized disclosures that let treasurers compare issuers the way they compare money market funds.
- [Interoperability standards take shape for institutional chains](https://kompositenews.com/blockchain/interoperability-standards-institutional-chains/): Messaging standards bodies and blockchain consortia are converging on formats that let regulated ledgers talk to each other, and to the systems banks already run.

## Newest stories

- [Anthropic's price range values it at up to $1.4tn](https://kompositenews.com/markets/anthropics-price-range-values-it-at-up-to-1-4tn/): Anthropic set an IPO range of $70-$78 for 825m shares, up to $64.35bn, plus a $26bn supplier placement. Our arithmetic on value, float and size.
- [Megaspeed's paper trail, from Commerce to the prosecutors](https://kompositenews.com/policy/megaspeeds-paper-trail-from-commerce-to-the-prosecutors/): DOJ asked Commerce to pause its Megaspeed chip probe after Nvidia contacted investigators, NBC reported. Our timeline of letters, cases and filings.
- [Canberra wants a regulator after OpenAI's agent got into Medicare data](https://kompositenews.com/ai/canberra-wants-a-regulator-after-openais-agent-got-into-medicare-data/): Australia plans a frontier AI regulator and accepts 18 review recommendations after an OpenAI agent reached a Medicare data portal. What it leaves open.
- [Tokenised assets up 9 per cent, fees up 28](https://kompositenews.com/crypto/tokenised-assets-up-9-per-cent-fees-up-28/): Securitize's Q3: revenue $18.6m, tokenised assets $4.8bn (+9%), a $66m loss, a $50m buyback, the River One deal and a Q2 volume cut to $4.4bn.
- [Nvidia's board opens an inquiry, 394 days after Megaspeed](https://kompositenews.com/ai/nvidia-board-opens-inquiry-394-days-after-megaspeed/): Nvidia's board opened an independent inquiry on 8 Nov into reports Jensen Huang was targeted by foreign intelligence. Our timeline and filing analysis.
- [A Microsoft redesign that earns IREN no delay credits](https://kompositenews.com/markets/a-microsoft-redesign-that-earns-iren-no-delay-credits/): IREN's 10-Q says a Microsoft-requested network change pushes delivery dates with no delay credits. Its $4bn ARR target moves to January or February.
- [Strategy sells common stock to buy back its preferred](https://kompositenews.com/crypto/strategy-sells-common-stock-to-buy-back-its-preferred/): Strategy's 9 Nov filing shows $188.3m of new-share money went to STRC buybacks and $81.9m to bitcoin. Our six-week tally: $1.16bn of buybacks.
- [The dealer quoted $1,270 for my Range Rover key. A locksmith charged $550](https://kompositenews.com/business/range-rover-key-dealer-quote-1270-locksmith-550/): A dealer quoted $1,270 for a replacement Range Rover key; a Pittsburgh mobile locksmith did it on-site for $550. Where the money goes, and how to vet a locksmith.
